implementation_notes: Kotlin ships lazy initialization as a library idiom: `val x by lazy { ... }` computes on first access and is synchronized by default (LazyThreadSafetyMode.SYNCHRONIZED), with PUBLICATION for idempotent initializers that may run more than once and NONE for provably single-threaded use (the delegate documentation states these modes). Shared state is an `object` declaration, initialized on first access with JVM class-initialization semantics, so no guard or counter is needed. The classic structure survives only as the choice of thread-safety mode and as care about recursive initialization.
pitfalls: The default lazy delegate synchronizes: every access performs a volatile/atomic check and a slow initializer blocks all readers; choose PUBLICATION or NONE deliberately, and never NONE where two threads can touch the value.
A lazy initializer that recursively reads the same property is undefined (throw or deadlock), and `by lazy` cannot be reset, so tests must not depend on replacing it.

An `object` initializer runs during class initialization of the file class: an exception in it leaves the object unusable (ExceptionInInitializerError), and heavy work adds latency to the first touch rather than to startup.
Companion-object state is a global under another name; reaching it through `Companion` does not make the dependency injectable or replaceable in tests.
